name: ACC1e-1-a-double-press-opens-a-second-guest-row
old: if (self.busy) return false;          // ONE PRESS IS ONE ACCOUNT
new: if (false) return false;          // ONE PRESS IS ONE ACCOUNT
note: Registering is TWO calls. A press between them opens a second guest row with no handle, no password and nothing that will ever adopt it.

name: ACC1e-2-the-guest-row-is-stranded-when-the-upgrade-fails
note: The session is kept BEFORE the upgrade is attempted on purpose: a `handle-taken` refusal leaves a real row this device owns, and dropping the secret would strand it and make the next press open another.

name: ACC1e-3-a-dead-credential-is-kept
note: A secret the service has stopped honouring is not a session; keeping it makes every later call fail the same way with nothing on screen saying why.

name: ACC1e-4-a-network-blip-signs-the-player-out
note: `offline` and `server` say NOTHING about whether the credential is good. Throwing a working session away over a bad second is a player signed out by a blip.

name: ACC1e-5-two-different-passwords-are-accepted
note: The service never sees `confirm` - it takes one password and has no idea a second box existed. This check exists here or nowhere, and without it a typo sets a password the player does not know.

name: ACC1e-6-a-password-is-trimmed-behind-the-players-back
note: A leading or trailing space is a character a player may have chosen. Trimming it here while the service hashes what it was sent is a login that works today and fails from another client tomorrow.

name: ACC1e-7-a-password-outlives-the-stage-that-asked-for-it
note: A password left in the flow is a password left in the DOM.

name: ACC1e-8-a-password-box-is-drawn-in-the-clear
note: Every password field, readable over a shoulder.

name: ACC1e-9-the-recovery-code-stage-gains-a-second-way-off
old: acts.append(act('I have written it down', () => flow.acknowledgeCode(), { primary: true }));
new:
acts.append(act('I have written it down', () => flow.acknowledgeCode(), { primary: true }));
      acts.append(act('Later', () => flow.go('in')));
note: The code is readable ONCE. A second way off that stage is a way to lose an account by taking it - and 'Later' is exactly the button somebody would add.

name: ACC1e-10-F1-the-ash-token-comes-back
note: ACC1e F1 put back verbatim: nothing declares --ash, so the declaration is invalid and every field label in the skin inherits --bone. The node pin walks the tokens; tools/accountCardProbe.mjs measures the computed colour and gets BONE.

name: ACC1e-11-the-card-wears-a-class-the-skin-does-not-style
note: An unstyled class draws as bare text in the middle of the enhanced skin and reads as a broken page rather than a missing rule.

name: ACC1e-12-a-refusal-word-reaches-the-player-raw
note: A player staring at `handle-frobnicated` has been told nothing.
